annotations.description: Kept a 2-land hand with only Swamps and no Green mana sources in a BG deck. Fierce Witchstalker (2GG) and Wolfkin Bond (4G) are completely uncastable without finding Forests, and Entomber Exarch (2BB) needs 4 lands. The hand is very land-light and completely missing the second color.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept the 7-card hand with 2 Swamps and no Forests
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 6 looking for a hand with both colors of mana and at least 2-3 lands. This hand has too high a risk of being stuck on 2 Swamps with uncastable green cards.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a 7-card hand that had 2 Swamps and three castable black cards (Mire Triton, Crow of Dark Tidings, Cemetery Recruitment) forming a functional curve. While Alpine Watchdog and Affa Guard Hound were dead without Plains, the black half of the hand was solid.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Mire Triton on turn 2 into Crow of Dark Tidings on turn 3 (if a land is drawn) provides a reasonable start, and Cemetery Recruitment adds card advantage. The white cards are dead weight initially but the black core is functional, and going to 6 risks a worse hand.

annotations.description: Discarded a Plains when the hand is land-light (only 2 Plains + 1 Swamp on board) and contains expensive spells (Gravedigger at 4 mana, Secure the Scene at 5 mana). Secure the Scene is the weakest card in hand since Pacifism already provides cheaper removal, and losing a land drop makes it harder to deploy the rest of the hand on curve.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Plains to Burglar Rat trigger
annotations.betterLine: Discard Secure the Scene — it's the most expensive and least efficient card in hand, redundant with Pacifism. Keeping both Plains ensures hitting land drops to cast Pack Leader on turn 3 and Gravedigger on turn 4.

annotations.description: MiniMx Contra cast Pacifism on a 1/1 Wight of Precinct Six before playing Thriving Moor. The Wight is currently just a 1/1 and while it could grow, using Pacifism on it is a relatively low-value removal target. More importantly, by casting Pacifism before playing the land, they used up their 2 mana and missed the opportunity to sequence properly. They should have played Thriving Moor first (it enters tapped so no mana this turn anyway, but it sets up future turns better). Additionally, Pacifism on a 1/1 that could be bounced or otherwise dealt with is questionable when they have Secure the Scene that can exile it permanently. However, the Wight could grow significantly as creatures die, so preemptively stopping it has some merit. The real issue is sequencing — they should have played the land first before casting the spell, though in this case it doesn't change available mana this turn since Thriving Moor enters tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pacifism on Wight of Precinct Six without first playing Thriving Moor
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor first (choosing green), then cast Pacifism. While the mana doesn't change this turn, playing land first is strictly better sequencing — it avoids revealing information unnecessarily and ensures the land drop isn't forgotten. Additionally, saving Pacifism for a bigger threat and just racing with Pack Leader while developing the board might be better long-term.

annotations.description: Chose Bounding Wolf over Entomber Exarch in precombat main phase. Bounding Wolf loses its flash advantage when cast at sorcery speed. Entomber Exarch could strip a removal spell from the opponent's hand (they have 4 cards), protecting future high-value plays like Fierce Witchstalker or Maalfeld Twins. With expensive threats waiting to be deployed, clearing the way with hand disruption could be more impactful than a slightly bigger body.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bounding Wolf (3/2) at sorcery speed, losing flash value
annotations.betterLine: Cast Entomber Exarch choosing the hand disruption mode to strip a noncreature card (likely removal) from opponent's hand, protecting future big plays

annotations.description: Cast Feat of Resistance proactively in precombat main phase for just a +1/+1 counter, when the opponent has no creatures to block and 6 cards in hand that could include removal. Feat of Resistance is far more valuable as instant-speed protection against removal than as a proactive +1/+1 counter. Since there are no blockers, the counter doesn't even help push more damage this turn beyond 1 extra.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Feat of Resistance targeting Pack Leader in precombat main phase with no immediate threat
annotations.betterLine: Hold Feat of Resistance as instant-speed protection. Attack with both creatures, and if opponent responds with removal, use Feat to protect. If no removal comes, save it for future turns. The +1/+1 counter is marginal compared to the protection value against the opponent's 6-card hand.

annotations.description: Cancelled the Entomber Exarch's ETB trigger, wasting either a free creature recursion (Bounding Wolf from graveyard) or hand disruption against the opponent. Both modes provide significant value, especially when behind 9 life to 20.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Cancel on Entomber Exarch's mandatory mode selection, wasting the ETB trigger entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Choose mode 1 to return Bounding Wolf (3/2 flash reach) from graveyard to hand for board stabilization, or mode 2 to strip a card from opponent's hand of 4 cards while gaining information.

annotations.description: Chose to make the opponent discard a noncreature card instead of returning Wight of Precinct Six from the graveyard. With 6 creature cards in the opponent's graveyard, Wight would be a 7/7 for just 1B — a game-changing threat when behind 9 to 20 life. The player had a Forest to play and could cast Wight next turn cheaply.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Cancel/mode 2 (opponent reveals hand and discards a noncreature card) on Entomber Exarch's ETB trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Choose mode 1 to return Wight of Precinct Six to hand, then cast it next turn as a 7/7 for 1B to stabilize the board.

annotations.description: Entomber Exarch's second mode requires choosing a noncreature card. Secure the Scene (a sorcery that exiles any nonland permanent) is the clear and likely only legal noncreature choice. Gravedigger is a creature card. Even if the game engine allowed picking any card, Secure the Scene is the most threatening card to GptOSS Villain since it could exile key permanents like a future Arlinn or Fierce Witchstalker.

annotations.betterLine: Choose Secure the Scene - it's the only noncreature card and also the most dangerous card to GptOSS Villain, being premium removal that could exile their best threats.

annotations.description: At 9 life facing 5 damage from Pack Leader (3/3) and Crow of Dark Tidings (2/1), declining to block with Entomber Exarch means taking all 5 damage and going to 4 life. Blocking Crow with Exarch would kill the Crow, keep the Exarch alive (2/2 vs 2/1), and only take 3 damage going to 6 life instead of 4. The Exarch's ETB has already been used so it's just a body.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 5 damage to go to 4 life
annotations.betterLine: Block Crow of Dark Tidings with Entomber Exarch to kill the Crow, preserve the Exarch, and only take 3 damage (going to 6 life instead of 4)

annotations.description: At 4 life, chose Wolfkin Bond (aura + 2/2 token) over Fierce Witchstalker (4/4 trample + Food token for life gain) or Wicked Wolf (removes the flying Crow threatening their low life total). The Food token from Witchstalker could gain 3 life (going to 7), which is critical at 4 life. Wolfkin Bond also creates aura vulnerability to removal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wolfkin Bond to enchant Entomber Exarch and create a 2/2 Wolf token
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fierce Witchstalker to get a 4/4 trample body and a Food token for desperately needed life gain at 4 life, or cast Wicked Wolf to fight and kill the Crow of Dark Tidings (a flying threat) while having Food synergy available later

annotations.description: Wolfkin Bond was placed on the opponent's Pack Leader, giving it +2/+2 (making it 5/5) instead of on their own Entomber Exarch. While the caster gets the 2/2 Wolf token either way, the +2/+2 buff goes to whatever creature is enchanted. At 4 life vs 20 life, buffing the opponent's creature is catastrophic - it makes the opponent's board much more threatening while the player desperately needs to stabilize.
annotations.actionTaken: Enchanted opponent's Pack Leader with Wolfkin Bond, giving the opponent a 5/5 creature
annotations.betterLine: Enchant own Entomber Exarch with Wolfkin Bond, creating a 4/4 and a 2/2 Wolf token on your side of the board

annotations.description: Opponent is at 4 life. Casting Affa Guard Hound (which becomes 3/3 due to Pack Leader's buff to Dogs) before combat guarantees lethal: attacking with Pack Leader (5/5), Crow of Dark Tidings (2/1 flying), and Affa Guard Hound (3/3) forces lethal damage since the opponent only has one non-sick blocker (Entomber Exarch 2/2) and can only block one ground attacker, while Crow flies over for 2. Without Affa Guard Hound, opponent can block Pack Leader with Exarch and survive at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Affa Guard Hound, missing guaranteed lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Affa Guard Hound precombat, then attack with Pack Leader, Crow of Dark Tidings, and Affa Guard Hound for guaranteed lethal regardless of how opponent blocks.

annotations.description: At 4 life, the player blocked Pack Leader with Entomber Exarch but left Crow of Dark Tidings (2/1) unblocked, taking 2 unnecessary damage (going to 2 life). The Wolf Token (which has summoning sickness but can still block) was available to block the Crow. Pack Leader's ability prevents combat damage to Dogs it controls, so the Exarch's damage to Pack Leader is irrelevant anyway - blocking Crow with the Wolf Token would have saved 2 life at no additional cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked only Pack Leader with Entomber Exarch, leaving Crow of Dark Tidings unblocked (taking 2 damage, going to 2 life)
annotations.betterLine: Block Pack Leader with Entomber Exarch AND block Crow of Dark Tidings with Wolf Token, taking 0 combat damage and staying at 4 life

annotations.description: Declined to cast Affa Guard Hound when opponent is at 2 life and all opponent's lands are tapped. The Hound would add a 2/2 body for free (exactly 3 mana available) providing redundancy against removal. While MiniMx likely has lethal next turn with Crow's flying, deploying an additional threat costs nothing and provides insurance against the opponent's 5 cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase without casting available spell
annotations.betterLine: Cast Affa Guard Hound for {2}{W}, adding a 2/2 body to the board and giving +0/+3 to a creature for protection. This provides an additional attacker as insurance in case the opponent removes or blocks existing threats.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing Pack Leader (5/8) and Crow of Dark Tidings (2/1), the player only blocked Pack Leader with Fierce Witchstalker, leaving Crow unblocked to deal 2 lethal damage. Both blockers (Wolf Token and Fierce Witchstalker) were available to block both attackers.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked only Pack Leader with Fierce Witchstalker, leaving Crow of Dark Tidings unblocked for lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Pack Leader with Fierce Witchstalker AND block Crow of Dark Tidings with Wolf Token. This prevents all combat damage to the player, keeping them alive at 2 life.
